item.title: Java 25 Security: Key Derivation Function API & PEM Encodings
item.description: Overview Java 25 ships two important security additions: JEP 510 — Key Derivation Function (KDF) API — Final. A standard API for HKDF, PBKDF2, and other KDFs. JEP 470 — PEM Encodings of Cryptographic Objects — Preview. Read and write .pem files without third-party libraries. These fill two long-standing gaps: Java had the underlying crypto but no clean standard API for key derivation and PEM I/O. Part 1: Key Derivation Function API (JEP 510) What Is Key Derivation?

item.title: Key Encapsulation Mechanism API (JEP 452): Post-Quantum Cryptography in Java
item.description: Why Post-Quantum Cryptography Now? Classical public-key cryptography (RSA, ECDH) relies on mathematical problems that are hard for classical computers — factoring large integers or solving the discrete logarithm problem. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer running Shor’s algorithm could solve these problems efficiently, breaking all existing RSA and ECC-based security. Quantum computers capable of breaking 2048-bit RSA don’t exist yet. But “harvest now, decrypt later” attacks are real: adversaries intercept and store encrypted traffic today, planning to decrypt it once quantum computers mature.
